claim: go-hass-agent maintainer joshuar stated verbatim in discussion #387 (Jan 18, 2025) that the systemctl service is intended primarily for headless server usage, and that running both a service instance and a desktop instance produces duplicate data.
stance_target: go-hass-agent is designed to be deployed as a headless systemd user service on servers, supporting adopt candidacy for fleet/server Linux hosts
scope_conditions: go-hass-agent deployment model; desktop vs headless Linux
quoted_support: The systemctl service is primarily for "headless" usage (i.e., servers) not running any desktop environment. If you run the agent both as a a systemctl service and in your desktop, you'll have two instances sending duplicate data, which might not be desired

claim: On desktop installs the maintainer recommends the desktop environment's autostart mechanism over a systemd service, because the service path and the desktop path serve different deployment models.
stance_target: Deployment guidance for go-hass-agent differs between desktop and server contexts
quoted_support: If you are running Go Hass Agent in a desktop, then you don't need to worry about configuring and starting it as a systemctl service. You can just use the autostart functionality of your desktop environment, for example in KDE or Gnome
